CVE-2026-102959.description:
The Grow R502-A fingerprint sensor driver (drivers/sensor/grow_r502a/grow_r502a.c) points drv_data->rx_buf.data at an rx_packet buffer on the caller's stack and enables the UART RX interrupt before waiting 1500 ms for a reply. When the wait timed out, transceive_packet() returned -ETIMEDOUT but left the RX interrupt enabled and rx_buf.data still pointing at the caller's buffer.

Once the caller's frame has returned, any bytes that arrive late on the UART are written by the interrupt handler uart_cb_handler() through the dangling pointer into stack memory that the thread has since reused. The bytes come from the device on the other end of the UART. An attacker with physical access who replaces or impersonates the fingerprint module can trigger this by delaying a reply past the timeout and then sending a packet. CVE-2026-120212.description:
Web::Simple versions before 0.037 for Perl do not escape single quotes in HTML::Tags output.

HTML::Tags and XML::Tags escape a plain string value by replacing only &, ", < and > with entities. A value interpolated into a single-quoted attribute, as in <a href='$value'>, can therefore close the attribute and add new ones, such as an event handler. Double-quoted attributes are not affected.

An attacker who controls a value that an application interpolates into a single-quoted attribute can inject script into the generated page.

CVE-2026-131210.title: SPL Injection through Finding Exclusion Rules in Splunk Enterprise Security
CVE-2026-131210.description:
In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the ueba_finding_exclusion_edit capability could create a finding exclusion rule that references an attacker-controlled lookup definition if the role also grants write access to globally shared lookup definitions, as the "ess_analyst" Splunk Enterprise Security role does. The User and Entity Behavior Analytics (UEBA) Content App could later include the lookup name in a search and run arbitrary Search Processing Language (SPL) commands with elevated permissions. For more information see Finding exclusions in Splunk Enterprise Security…

CVE-2026-99770.title: drm/vc4: Publish the output fence outside of job_lock
CVE-2026-99770.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/vc4: Publish the output fence outside of job_lock

job_lock is taken by the V3D interrupt handler, so nesting an IRQ-unsafe
lock under it creates an inversion. drm_syncobj_replace_fence() takes
drm_syncobj::lock, which other paths acquire with interrupts enabled. For
example, a thread interrupted while holding it blocks the handler on
job_lock, and the handler can only make progress once the submit path
releases job_lock, which it cannot do while waiting for drm_syncobj::lock.

CVE-2026-99811.title: vfio/cdx: prevent read-only region mappings from becoming writable
CVE-2026-99811.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

vfio/cdx: prevent read-only region mappings from becoming writable

vfio_cdx_mmap() rejects writable mappings of regions without the WRITE
flag, but leaves VM_MAYWRITE set. Userspace can map such a region
read-only and then upgrade the mapping to writable with mprotect(),
writing to MMIO regions the device marks read-only.

Clear VM_MAYWRITE for regions without the WRITE flag, as i915 does for
its read-only objects and as fixed in drm/vc4 (CVE-2026-68445),
drm/panthor (CVE-2024-53071) and commit a5edadbae57e ("ptp: vmclock:
prevent read-only mappings from becoming writable").

Note this is defensive hardening: no in-tree cdx device currently
publishes a region without the WRITE flag. The guard costs nothing and
keeps the mmap() interface honest if a read-only region ever appears.
